title: § 752 Debt
subject: Partnership Tax
note: Starter pack. Rules come from the Code and Treasury Regulations, not from your outline. All facts are practice hypotheticals.

questions.assumption: 50/50 general partners who share losses equally, so each bears half the economic risk of loss on the mortgage.
questions.prompt: What is Ben's outside basis, and does he recognize gain?

explain.rule: § 752(b): a decrease in a partner's individual liabilities because the partnership assumes them is a deemed cash distribution. § 752(a): an increase in his share of partnership liabilities is a deemed cash contribution. Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) nets the two.
explain.application: $60,000 basis − $40,000 relieved + $20,000 share (50%) = $40,000. The net decrease is $20,000, which is less than his $60,000 basis, so § 731(a)(1) triggers no gain.
explain.takeaway: Subtract the full debt, then add back your share.

whyWrong: This ignores the $40,000 of debt relief entirely.
This subtracts the debt but never adds back Ben's $20,000 share under § 752(a).
Gain arises only if the net deemed distribution ($20,000) exceeds basis ($60,000). It doesn't.

questions.assumption: Each partner bears half the economic risk of loss on the mortgage.

explain.rule: § 722 gives Cara basis equal to the cash she contributed. § 752(a) treats her increased share of partnership liabilities as a further cash contribution.
explain.takeaway: Every partner who picks up a debt share gets a basis increase, not just the contributor.

whyWrong: This misses Cara's $20,000 share of the mortgage.
Cara picks up only her share ($20,000), not the full $40,000.
Cara isn't relieved of any debt; her basis can't go below her cash contribution here.

questions.assumption: 50/50 partnership; each partner bears half the economic risk of loss on the debt.
questions.prompt: How much gain does Gus recognize, and what is his outside basis afterward?

explain.rule: Under § 752(b) and Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f), the net decrease in a partner's liabilities is a deemed cash distribution. Under § 731(a)(1), cash in excess of outside basis is gain from the sale of a partnership interest.
explain.application: Relieved of $30,000; picks up $15,000. Net deemed distribution is $15,000 against a $10,000 basis, which gives $5,000 of gain and leaves basis at $0.
explain.takeaway: Net debt relief over basis = gain. Basis never goes below zero.

whyWrong: The $15,000 net deemed distribution exceeds Gus's $10,000 basis, so there is gain.
$20,000 would be relief over basis without adding back Gus's $15,000 share.
$15,000 is the net deemed distribution, not the gain. Gain is the excess over basis.

questions.assumption: General partnership; losses shared 60% A / 40% B; partners must restore deficits under state law.
questions.prompt: What is A's share of the $100,000 recourse liability?

explain.rule: A partner's share of a recourse liability equals the economic risk of loss he bears, measured by a constructive liquidation: all assets are treated as worthless, the loss is allocated, and the partner with a deficit would have to pay it. Treas. Reg. § 1.752-2(b).
explain.takeaway: Recourse debt follows who pays in a worst-case liquidation.

whyWrong: Recourse debt isn't split per capita; it follows economic risk of loss.
A bears only his deficit, not the whole debt.
$40,000 is B's share.

questions.assumption: 50/50 partnership; tier 3 follows profit shares; § 704(c) traditional method.
questions.prompt: What is A's share of the $50,000 nonrecourse liability right after formation?

explain.rule: Treas. Reg. § 1.752-3(a): tier 1 = share of partnership minimum gain; tier 2 = the § 704(c) gain the partner would get if the property were sold for the debt; tier 3 = the rest, by profit shares.
explain.application: Tier 1: debt $50,000 − book value $100,000 → $0. Tier 2: a sale for $50,000 gives $30,000 of tax gain, all to A under § 704(c) → $30,000. Tier 3: remaining $20,000 split 50/50 → $10,000. A's share = $40,000.
explain.takeaway: Tier 2 shifts nonrecourse debt toward the partner with built-in gain.

whyWrong: $25,000 skips tier 2 and splits everything 50/50.
A doesn't get the whole liability; tier 3 gives B part of it.
$30,000 is only tier 2; it leaves out A's tier 3 share.

questions.topic: Sale of an interest: debt relief
facts: Ivy sells her interest for cash
questions.prompt: What is Ivy's gain or loss on the sale?

explain.rule: § 752(d): liabilities are treated as in a sale of property not associated with partnerships, so the seller's amount realized includes the liabilities she is relieved of (Treas. Reg. § 1.1001-2). Gain is capital under § 741 absent § 751 assets.
explain.takeaway: Debt relief is part of the price.

whyWrong: This leaves debt relief out of the amount realized while keeping it in basis.
This ignores Ivy's $35,000 basis.
$50,000 is the amount realized, not the gain.

facts: Partnership pays down a recourse loan; Jo's share falls by
choices: Nothing; debt changes don't affect partners

explain.rule: § 752(b): a decrease in a partner's share of partnership liabilities is a deemed cash distribution. § 731(a)(1): cash over basis is gain; § 733 reduces basis, but not below zero.
explain.application: Deemed distribution $8,000 against $5,000 basis gives $3,000 of gain; basis goes to $0.
explain.takeaway: Shrinking your debt share is like getting cash.

whyWrong: § 752(b) treats the decrease as a cash distribution.
Outside basis can't go below zero; the excess is gain.
Only the excess over basis ($3,000) is gain, and basis drops to $0.

questions.prompt: Practice hypothetical: Gus contributes property with a $10,000 basis and a $50,000 FMV, subject to a $30,000 recourse debt the partnership assumes. Hana contributes $20,000 cash. They are 50/50 partners and each bears half the economic risk of loss on the debt. Analyze the tax consequences to Gus and to Hana: gain recognized, character, and each partner's outside basis. Also give Gus's book and tax capital accounts.

rubric.model: Issue: Does the debt shift trigger gain, and what are the partners' bases? Rule: § 721 nonrecognition; § 722 basis; § 752(b) relief of liabilities = deemed distribution; § 752(a) increase = deemed contribution; Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) netting; § 731(a)(1) gain when deemed cash exceeds basis; § 733 basis reduction. Application: Gus is relieved of $30,000 and picks up $15,000, a net $15,000 deemed distribution against a $10,000 basis, giving $5,000 of gain (treated as gain from sale of his partnership interest, generally capital) and $0 outside basis. Hana: $20,000 cash + $15,000 debt share = $35,000. Gus's book capital: $50,000 − $30,000 = $20,000; tax capital: $10,000 − $30,000 = −$20,000. Outside basis ($0) is $5,000 more than tax capital plus his debt share (−$20,000 + $15,000 = −$5,000) because Gus recognized $5,000 of gain. Conclusion: Gus recognizes $5,000 of gain and has $0 basis; Hana recognizes nothing and has $35,000 basis.
